answer: Use a memory-hard proof-of-work puzzle bound to each key and renewed every epoch. The registry sends a fresh random seed; the agent must run a cipher-like scrypt hash needing 2 GB of RAM for about ten minutes and submit the result, which any verifier checks in milliseconds. Because the seed includes the public key, work cannot be shared or reused. A sonnet-length proof gets posted to the ledger, and peers echo it to confirm. Each fake rents its own memory and compute, costing roughly eight dollars monthly.
